title.title: Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem
title.subtitle: Claim: a smooth volume-preserving map of the 3-torus whose single orbit $f \circ T^n$ is an orthonormal basis

panels.caption: $\langle f \circ T^m, f \circ T^n \rangle$ for $m, n$ from $-3$ to $3$

lines.tex: \{\, f \circ T^n : n \in \mathbb Z \,\}\ \text{ is an orthonormal basis of } L^2_0

beats.text: Inner products along one orbit $f \circ T^n$: the identity matrix
And complete: one orbit spans everything. Bernoulli shifts need infinitely many
Built from smooth twists of the 3-torus

There is a C-infinity diffeomorphism T of the 3-torus preserving Lebesgue volume
The paper itself says the historical real-line question recorded by Ulam differs from the probability-space form solved here.

plain: Stir a box smoothly: can one pattern, stirred again and again, spell out every other pattern exactly once?

steps: Start from simple smooth twists of the three-dimensional torus
Conjugate each new twist so the signal's pieces line up
In the limit, one orbit is a complete set of perpendicular directions

data.result: one orbit $f \circ T^n$: an orthonormal basis

voice.text: Shift one pattern over and over: the copies are perpendicular, and they fill everything.
Built as a limit of smooth twists, each nudged so the copies line up.
Claimed: Banach's simple spectrum, realized smoothly.
